404 Media previously reported a flaw in the iCloud+ "Hide My Email" feature that allowed anyone to obtain a user's real email address. Apple now says the issue has officially been fixed.

Apple says the security flaw in Hide My Email was fixed earlier this month

If you are an iCloud+ or Apple One subscriber, Apple's Hide My Email privacy feature can be a great way to protect your real email address.

Here's how Apple describes how it works on its official website:

However, according to a recent report from 404 Media, Hide My Email has long had a flaw that could let anyone get hold of the real email address linked to an Apple account. The disclosure has also prompted a new proposed lawsuit.

Apple said today that the flaw was officially fixed earlier this month.

Apple told 404 Media that the company "rolled out a fix on July 3, and said the issue was fully resolved."

The iCloud+ flaw was initially reported to Apple by Tyler Murphy in June 2025. After initial discussions, Apple claimed it had been fixed, but Murphy later discovered the issue was still present. Hopefully this time it has truly been resolved for good.

How often do you use the Hide My Email feature in iCloud+? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
